summary: Lawns, play corners and shaded benches right on Saputara Lake's shore.
description:
The Lake Garden runs along Saputara Lake's shore, all broad lawns, old shade trees, flower borders, a children's play corner and benches angled at the water. Its job is simple: absorb the families that spill off the boats, and it does it well, especially in the soft hour before sunset when the lake mirrors the ridge and the town's day-trippers settle onto the grass.

Because it is level and adjacent to everything, this is the easiest green space in town for elderly visitors and prams. Vendors work the gate; the promenade connects onward to the boat club and the Nageshwar temple, so the garden folds naturally into the standard lakefront hour rather than demanding its own slot.
highlights: Lawns and shade directly on the lakeshore
Level paths, the easiest garden in town
